subject: Acme Retail POC: semantic search call recap + model recommendations and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Acme Retail POC: semantic search call recap + model recommendations and next steps

Hi Samira (and Acme DS team),

Thanks again for taking time today — good overview of your search use cases (product-title matching, faceted recommendations, and closed-loop reranking). Quick recap and proposed plan so we have alignment: 

What we heard
- Primary objective: improve search recall and relevance for long-tail SKUs and customer-entered queries.
- Data available: ~3M catalog records, product titles/descriptions, historical click logs (sample provided), and curated seed relevance labels (~1k).
- SLA: online nearest-neighbor latency target ~40ms 95p for top-100 retrieval in prod.
- Concern: model drift over seasonal assortments and embedding dimensionality affecting index size/cost.

Preliminary evaluation highlights (model candidates we discussed)
- Model A (rwd-sem-1, 1024-d): Recall@10 0.81, MRR 0.44, index size ~6.2GB per shard (est) — strong for titles but slightly less separation on long descriptions.
- Model B (open-fast-768): Recall@10 0.75, MRR 0.39, smaller index footprint but lower recall on synonyms.
- Model C (big-embed-1536-quant): Recall@10 0.84, MRR 0.48, better separation but larger index and added CPU/GPU cost for quantized vectors.

Attached I dropped our initial CSV with the per-query metrics and the prompt/label set we used for the POC. These are small sample runs — not final.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme-embeddings-eval-20260712.csv (CSV, 42KB)], [Attachment: acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (JSONL, 120KB)]

Suggested immediate next steps (agreed on call):
1) Redwood to run a 3-way evaluation across A/B/C on your full seed label set (we'll produce recall@k, MRR, nDCG, mean intra-cluster similarity, and PCA-based dimensionality diagnostics). Rishi to lead.
2) Acme to share a sanitized sample of 100k catalog rows + 10k recent queries for drift baseline (Samira).
3) Align on index strategy: 1024-d vs 1536-d tradeoffs; potential quantization profiles to hit your latency & storage targets.
4) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next Tue to review results and agree on pilot scope.

Open questions we need help on from Acme:
- Is your on-prem search cluster able to store shards of 6–8GB per node or should we optimize for 768-d footprint?
- Acceptable drift threshold (how often do you want us to surface regressions — weekly/monthly?).

Proposed timeline
- 7/12–7/16: run full eval (Redwood)
- 7/16–7/19: internal review and quick cost estimate for Dedicated capacity for pilot
- 7/20: demo of pilot results + recommendation

If that all sounds right, I’ll start the eval run and loop Rishi.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Acme Retail POC: semantic search call recap + model recommendations and next steps

Thanks Ben — this is great and captures the call. A couple of quick clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide the sanitized sample tomorrow (7/13) — I’ll drop a share link for 100k rows and the 10k queries.
- On drift thresholds: our internal SREs currently flag anything >2% month-over-month change in average query->click distance; we’d prefer weekly nudges if you detect sustained drift >1%.
- For the index footprint question — our AWSElastic cluster has nodes with ~12GB of RAM available for vector shards but storage is limited on hot tier, so the 6–8GB per shard estimate is OK but we’d like to explore quantized 16-bit options.

Also attaching a short note on label provenance (how they created the 1k seed relevance labels) — that should help with eval weighting.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme-label-provenance.pdf (PDF, 28KB)], [Attachment: acme-sample-share-link.txt (text, 1KB)]

Happy with the proposed timeline. Please go ahead with the eval and we’ll share the sample by EOD tomorrow.

—Samira

Ben / Rishi — quick internal note from a pricing/procurement perspective before we run a bunch of evals: 

- If Acme wants to pilot with Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) we should prepare a 30-day pilot quote vs hosted pay-as-you-go. For pilot sizing I want both a 1024-d and 1536-d cost estimate (storage + inferred per-embedding compute).
- We should also produce a risk note on quality regressions: if we change to a smaller-dim model later (to save cost), recall dropouts for certain categories (e.g., seasonal SKUs) were visible in the sample. We should quantify category-level deltas and expose them in the dashboard.

Action items for Rishi (priority):
1) Include category-level recall@10 deltas in the output CSV so we can call out any segments that deteriorate.
2) Run one quantized profile (16-bit) for model C to compare storage and recall tradeoffs.
3) Estimate per-embedding cost per 1M items for both 1024-d and 1536-d options (rough ballpark OK for pilot).

Marissa

Subject: Request: short evaluation run for Acme (3 model candidates, category deltas, quantized profile)

Rishi — please prioritize the 3 tasks below so we can deliver to Acme by EOD 7/16. Samira is sharing the 100k sample tomorrow. Keep outputs in the shared Drive link and ping me when the jobs start.

Evaluation tasks (deliverables to include CSV + short readme):
A) Run models A/B/C from the call against acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (attached). Compute per-query Recall@1/5/10, MRR, nDCG@10, mean intra-cluster cosine similarity, and mean pairwise distance.
B) Produce category-level recall@10 deltas vs baseline (baseline = current BM25+heuristics measurements in acme-embeddings-eval-20260712.csv) — highlight any category with delta <= -0.05.
C) Run quantized 16-bit profile for model C and report recall/mRR tradeoffs and index size estimate.

Priority notes:
- Keep random seed fixed so results are reproducible.
- Use cosine similarity by default but compute dot-product results as a check (Acme asked about both).
- Include PCA scree plot data (we only need the explained variance numbers) to inform dimensionality tradeoffs.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-candidate-models-shortlist.md (MD, 6KB)], [Attachment: acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (JSONL, 120KB)]

Thanks — I’ll coordinate timing with Samira for the 30-min follow-up next Tue.
